summary: The vertex-degree formula is the standard Wythoff vertex-figure count, and the balance law follows at once from the transitive action of the symmetry group on Weyl chambers together with the fact that the symmetry group contains a map sending f to -f, or acts by a diagram automorphism that does. The perturbed 16-cell example only shows that the symmetry is needed. No research audience is established for this as a result in its own right.

findings.message: Trivial or routine: (a) counts the edges at a vertex as the orbits of the vertex stabiliser W_U on the edges for each ringed node, which is classical Wythoff/Coxeter material. (b) follows because every edge is parallel to a root, so the sweep's combinatorics is constant on Weyl chambers; W permutes the chambers transitively, and f and -f lie in symmetric chambers. Neither part is shown to go beyond a textbook exercise in Coxeter-group polytopes.

internal_notes.message: I found no source that states the exact degree formula in this notation, but the vertex-figure rule from Coxeter diagrams (remove the ringed node and ring its neighbours, etc.) is standard (Coxeter, Regular Polytopes; Klitzing). I could not retrieve Champagne-Kjiri-Patera-Sharp (1995), which counts faces with decorated diagrams. The sweep/h-vector link is classical (Lee; Buchstaber-Panov). Literature is low because the candidate cites no Wythoff, Coxeter or sweep sources.

what_would_reach_4: A non-obvious consequence, such as a new inequality or classification for sweeps of non-simple or non-Wythoffian polytopes that does not reduce to chamber transitivity, written up against Coxeter, Lee and Champagne-Kjiri-Patera-Sharp.

summary: A computed census (35 combinatorial types, 60 window tiles, 69 vertex configurations) of one hyperplane section of the A4* permutohedron honeycomb. The rank-2 periodicity is immediate: the entries of u span Q(phi), which has dimension 2 over Q, so the lattice vectors orthogonal to u form a rank 2 sublattice. Sections and projections of periodic tilings are the standard cut-and-project setting. Paper-worthiness and an audience are not established for this specific census.

findings.message: The exact rank-2 period lattice is an elementary consequence of the Q-span of the coordinates of u (rank 2), so it carries no independent weight. The rest is a finite enumeration for one chosen slope. It is not compared with the cut-and-project and model-set literature or with known A4/golden projections, and no consequence of interest to quasicrystal or tiling researchers (for example a substitution rule, a window description or a diffraction statement) is given.

internal_notes.message: I found no prior source for this exact slice. Koca et al. project the A4 permutohedron to the Coxeter plane with golden scaling (2D), which is the nearest comparator. A slice that is periodic in rank 2 and aperiodic in the third direction sits between periodic and quasiperiodic structure, and tiling theorists might find that mildly interesting. Hence 3 rather than 2, but it is still below the floor.

what_would_reach_4: Identify the slice as a model set with an explicit window and prove a structural property (a substitution/inflation rule, pure point diffraction, or a classification over all slopes in Q(phi)^5), with the counts as corollaries, and compare with the de Bruijn/Baake-Grimm framework.

summary: An enumeration of the unit-edge members of the deformation cones of three Coxeter permutohedra. The characterisation (0/1 edge labels that close around every 2-face) is the standard description of deformations by edge lengths satisfying the 2-face closing conditions, restricted to lengths 0/1. The counts 17/101/4427 are computational data, and no structural theorem or audience is established.

findings.message: The characterisation follows directly from the edge-length (closing-condition) description of type cones used by Postnikov and by Ardila-Castillo-Eur-Postnikov for Coxeter permutohedra. What remains is three orbit counts with no general formula, structure or application, so paper-worthiness is not demonstrated.

internal_notes.message: I found no prior enumeration of equilateral deformed Coxeter permutohedra. Unit-edge generalized permutohedra link to matroid polytopes when restricted to 0/1 lengths in type A, and the counts may relate to known objects (for example matroid-like or Coxeter-matroid polytopes), but I did not establish this. Neutral novelty; low research interest as stated.

what_would_reach_4: A structural identification of the 0/1 wall labellings (for example a bijection with Coxeter matroids or another known family) holding for all finite Coxeter groups, with the three counts as checked instances.

summary: A graphical zonotope is generated by the vectors e_i - e_j of a graph, which represent the regular (graphic) matroid. Shephard's theorem then gives translative tiling of the affine span for any positive generator lengths. The n = 4 list is a direct check. Note that there are six connected graphs on four vertices; the two trees both give the cube, so the five parallelohedra correspond to five isomorphism classes of graphic matroids, not five connected graphs.

findings.message: Trivial or routine: immediate from Shephard (1974) and McMullen on space-tiling zonotopes (zonotope tiles iff its matroid is regular; graphic matroids are regular). The phrase 'the five connected graphs on 4 vertices' is inaccurate: there are six (path, star, paw, 4-cycle, diamond, K4), and the path and star both give the cube.

internal_notes.message: The 4D zonotopal parallelotopes are classified as graphic subsystems of K5 plus cographic K3,3*, which already embeds the graph/zonotope dictionary. The search summary attributes the regular-matroid criterion to Shephard; I did not inspect the primary paper (behind a paywall).

what_would_reach_4: Nothing in this direction; the statement is a known corollary. A new result would need to concern non-zonotopal deformations of graphical zonotopes (for example which deformed graphical zonotopes tile, in line with Padrol-Pilaud-Poullot).

summary: The interpolation from the permutohedron to Loday's associahedron lies in the deformation cone. The face lattice is preserved for t < 1 because the open type cone of the braid fan is convex and the associahedron lies on a boundary face of its closure. The facets that vanish at t = 1 are exactly the non-interval facets, as in Postnikov and Hohlweg-Lange. The non-tiling for t > 0 and the equal-speed vanishing thresholds are short computations.

findings.message: Routine: preserving the face lattice along the segment and the simultaneous vanishing of non-interval facets at the endpoint follow from the convexity of the type cone and the standard description of Loday's associahedron as a deformed permutohedron obtained by moving facets (Postnikov 2009; Hohlweg-Lange). The tiling claim is unattributed and is not compared with the classification of parallelohedra among generalized permutohedra.

internal_notes.message: The Padrol-Pilaud-Poullot PDF URL returned 404. The formula D_S = sum k_b k_b' may be new in this exact form, but it is an elementary computation of support functions.

what_would_reach_4: A general theorem on segments in type cones (for example a classification of which deformed permutohedra tile by translation, or the face-lattice jump for all nested-complex polytopes) with the associahedron as one instance.

summary: Brute-force Hamiltonian-cycle counts on small graphs. 44 for the truncated octahedron is already in OEIS A343433. Polster-Ross state that there are 10,792 Minimus extents, which equals 2 x 5396 directed traversals, so the total of 5396 cycles is effectively known. The class counts, periodicity and D3d-symmetric classes are new data at most, of recreational/change-ringing interest, with no established research audience.

findings.message: Omitted prior results: the truncated octahedron count of 44 is OEIS A343433, and the 10,792 Minimus extents (= 5396 undirected Hamiltonian cycles) appear in Polster-Ross (Plus Magazine). Presenting these as theorems without attribution changes the public account. The remaining orbit and symmetry counts are finite enumerations without a research question.

internal_notes.message: The 5396 total assumes the same transition graph (all four Minimus changes x, 12, 14, 34). The match of 10792/2 strongly suggests that it is the same graph. The White 'Ringing the cosets' tradition (Amer. Math. Monthly 1987; Proc. Camb. Phil. Soc.) is the research context for change ringing and should be cited.

what_would_reach_4: A general theorem, for example on extents with prescribed symmetry for n bells, or a structural classification of periodic change words, placed in White's coset framework, rather than counts for n = 4.
